players.note: Brooks was the LB1 overall last season and enters the season expected to be a part of the weekly LB3 conversation. With a plus matchup on tap for Week 1 against the Las Vegas Raiders, he is also the IDP1. Start him everywhere.

Jack Campbell remains locked in as a top-five option for the 2026 season, regardless of opponent. He was an absolute monster in 2025 and should pick up right where he left off in Week 1 against New Orleans.

Carson forced his way into the LB1 conversation as a rookie and will now vie for the LB1 overall title. Schwesinger should be a fixture in your starting lineup, including this week against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Blake Cashman is a top-15 option for Week 1, thanks to a plus matchup against the Green Bay Packers. The LB8 in fppg last season, Cashman will produce at a high enough level to be back in that mix in 2026. Start Cashman as an LB1 option regardless of opponent, including this week against the Green Bay Packers.

Roquan Smith is in line for a big game against Jonathan Taylor and the Indianapolis Colts. Roquan should not lack for tackle opportunities and will look to make good on his near universal top-five linebacker ranking for Week 1.

Foye is no longer the tackle machine he once was, but he still makes for an excellent LB1 option and becomes an excellent LB1 play when he has plus matchups, as he does this week against the Cleveland Browns. Look for Oluokun to create havoc against Deshaun Watson and the Browns offense.
Ernest Jones remains locked in as a top-10 option for Week 1. Fire him up as you normally would for a plus matchup against New England.

Nick Bolton is an easy LB1 play for a plus Week 1 matchup against division rival Denver Broncos. Bolton averaged 5.5 solo tackles against Denver last season and may see that number jump against what should be an improved and more consistent Broncos offense.

Zack Baun remains in the weekly LB1 mix for Week 1. Things may change as the season progresses and Jihaad Campbell becomes more consistent, but Baun is a top-12 option for a plus matchup against Washington in Week 1.

Criminally underrated despite being the LB6 last season, Nate Landman is a locked-in LB1 option for Week 1. Landman should see a heavy workload despite the improvement up front, thanks to the 49ers' offensive scheme. Landman will be an LB1 option until further notice.

Quay Walker could have a monster performance in store for IDP managers in Week 1 against what should be an exploitable Miami Dolphins offense. Expect LB1 numbers from the former Green Bay Packer who should play nearly every snap for the black and silver.

Fred Warner is locked in as a top-five option for what should be a busy night against the Los Angeles Rams offense. There are few as good at the position as Warner is at just about everything the position asks him to do. Start him with confidence weekly regardless of matchup.
Singleton remains a strong LB2 option to open the season, especially given the plus matchup against a familiar foe in the Kansas City Chiefs. Start him with confidence as a top-25 option.

Cooper projects as a comfortable LB2 play this season but has flashed the upside to make his way into the Lb1 conversation before the season is over. Fire him up as an Lb2 with top-15 upside for a plus Week 1 matchup against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings.

Robert Spillane is an easy LB2 play for what should be a busy night against the run against Seattle in Week 1. Spillane is no longer the lock for top-12 numbers every week, but deserves to be a part of the top-15 conversation when given plus matchups like he has this week.

Zaire Franklin in Green Bay could be massive for his IDP value, but for now he should still be viewed as an LB2 option that you probably have rostered as your LB3 or LB4. Start Zaire where possible for a plus Week 1 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

Azeez Al-Shaair has every week LB2 upside, but should be treated as more of an LB3/flex option until he shows he can be consistent enough to trust with a more prominent role for your fantasy squad. The matchup is appealing against Buffalo, making him someone ot slide into your flex if you have comparable options currently blocking him.

Sonny Styles is an interesting start for Week 1. He has a lower floor than his draft position suggests but is teeming with upside. The matchup is appealing enough to throw caution to the wind and plug him into lineups, even in two linebacker builds. Treat him as a top-20 option for Week 1, thanks to a plus matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Daiyan Henley is locked in as an LB2 option for a plus Week 1 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Henley should see a heavy dose of the run and enough action in the middle of the field to have a monster night. Fire Henley up as part of the top-15 conversation. 
'

Cedric Gray was excellent in 2025, finishing the season as the LB5 overall despite missing a game. Locked in as a weekly LB1 option, Gray would look to become a household IDP name this season. Tap him as a top-five option for a plus Week 1 matchup against the New York Jets.

CJ Allen is an intriguing LB2 play for Week 1. He profiles with massive upside, but snap share question marks keep him out of the LB1 conversation. Tap him as an upside LB2 play for a plus Week 1 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

Still flying a bit under the radar, Drake Thomas is part of the LB2 conversation for Week 1. He flashed LB1 upside at times last season and just needs to stay consistent to start being mentioned in the same conversation as teammate Ernest Jones.

Avrell Reese could have a monster season in store for fantasy managers. While edge is more valuable, he always projected as the most impactful as a pass rushing middle linebacker who can be used in the early career Micah Parsons role. He will have a chance to shine on Sunday Night Football and expected to see multiple pass rush opportunities alongside the Giants trio of gamewreckers on the edge. Start Reese as an LB2 with an LB4 floor.

Myles Garrett checks in as the number one DL option for Week 1. Yes, Aaron Donald has been ruled out, but that doesn't change the fact that this is the most talented line the future Hall of Famer has ever been a part of. Look for the Rams to find a way to ensure that Garrett gets to Brock Purdy at least once in the Land Down Under.
Christian Elliss should remain on benches for Week 1. His snap share remains uncertain, and he is on your roster for the byes and as injury depth. Sit him outside of 20+ team leagues.

Dre Greenlaw profiles as a weekly top-25 option, and that is even more true this week thanks to a plus matchup against the San Grabnciso 49ers. Fire the fiery 49ers linebacker up as a high upside LB2 play.

Cody Simon lost the battle for the starting job to Jack Gibbens. Simon was the favorite to win the job, but Gibbens, a veteran NFL starter proved to be the superior option, at least for now. Stash Simon where bench space allows, but those in shallower formats should move on completely once a better option emerges.
Leave Omar Speights on fantasy benches for the time being. While he is officially listed as a starter, he may not see the field enough to be fantasy relevant in the Rams' defensive scheme.

Byron Young remains the biggest beneficiary from the addition of Myles Garrett (and eventually Aaron Donald). While Jared Verse rightfully commanded more attention and pushed pockets toward Young, Young registered 10 of his 12 sacks against left tackles, something he will rarely be asked to do this season with Myles Garrett being a left tackle-destroying monster through and through. Tap Byron Young as a top-10 option for Week 1.

Dre'Mont Jones is on double-digit sack watch, and it starts on Wednesday night against Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks. He should be back on the edge full time under Vrabel and should really start to cause havoc when former Titans teammate Harold Landry gets activated from the PUP list later this season. Tap Jones as an upside DL2 play for a neutral matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

Keion White is slated to get the start opposite Nick Bosa in Week 1, but is not much of a fantasy option outside of sack heavy leagues. The Rams scheme and offensive line combination ranks them as one of the better units in the league, so you do not want to be plugging in someone who is only on your roster as emergency depth in Week 1. Look elsewhere for your DL3.
